title: I didn’t see last season’s “All In” but after grossing $1.5M a week I...
transcript: Let's talk about all out, which is Broadway's latest celebrity vehicle. It features a rotating cast of celebrities. People like John Stuart, Ray Romano, Jenny Slate. My cast featured a lineup of Wayne Brady, Jim Gaffigan, Cecily Strong and Ben Schwartz. It also features quite a bit of music by the band Lawrence, who are performing at every show. And I believe it's all music from their most recent album. And if you don't know, the central conceit of the show is that the four celebrities at a given performance will sit down in chairs and they will recite these short stories by author Simon Rich. They do all have binders with the stories written down that they can reference if they need. However, I will say at my performance, they were very much off book. But this is not a play in the traditional sense. And there is no overarching narrative besides the fact that all of the stories have to do with ambition. And the stories themselves are fine. Actually really liked the first couple stories. They were really funny, really short and snappy. But as the show gets on, these stories get longer. And they also get less funny. As the show is trying to deliver some pathos in addition to the comedy. But I don't think it really struck that balance well enough. And there were long stretches of the show that I think could have had more laughs. The four celebrities all did great with The material they were given. If anything, I thought they elevated it, but overall, I thought it was just okay. The best part of the show by far, in my opinion, is the music by Lawrence. I was not super familiar with their music prior to seeing the show, although I was a big fan of Gracie's performance in the last seasons. Just in time. But I thought all of the music was really fun, and Gracie's voice is just insane. And I really appreciated how they used the set and how the set was able to seamlessly transform from this, like, 1970s office into a concert space. It really created a juxtaposition between these higher energy, dynamic musical performances and the comparatively lower energy and more subdued stories. And I just don't know that that juxtaposition really worked. It felt like watching two shows at once. So overall, would I recommend it? Maybe. I mean, if you are a big fan of one of the celebrities or even Lawrence, I think you'll have a good enough time. But if you choose to skip it, I also don't know if you're missing out that much.
classificationReason: Creator attended a performance (describes their specific cast: Wayne Brady, Jim Gaffigan, Cecily Strong, Ben Schwartz) and shares opinions on the show's stories and structure. Title explicitly distinguishes this from last season's 'All In,' confirming this is All Out: Comedy About Ambition (all-out-2025).
